title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique spiritual and community-driven traditions that define the Royal experience at Bethel University in Minnesota.

cards.title: Vespers Sunday Night Worship
cards.subtitle: A student-led musical worship tradition since the 1980s
cards.notes: Gather at Benson Great Hall every Sunday at 9 p.m. for an hour of student-led music and prayer. It is a cornerstone of spiritual life on campus.
cards.short_summary: A weekly, student-led musical worship service that has been a staple of Bethel spiritual life for over 30 years.
cards.evidence_claim: Vespers is a weekly musical worship service formed by students in the 1980s, held every Sunday night at 9 p.m. in Benson Great Hall.
cards.source_title: What Does Vespers Mean to Bethel Students?
cards.access_notes: Open to students, alumni, and the community; held Sunday nights during the academic semester.

cards.title: Broomball Under the Lights
cards.subtitle: The signature winter intramural sport
cards.notes: Join a team in January to play this hockey-like sport using brooms and a ball on the campus ice rinks. It is a decades-old winter tradition.
cards.short_summary: A beloved winter tradition where students compete in intramural broomball leagues on campus ice rinks during the cold Minnesota months.
cards.evidence_claim: Broomball is a favorite Bethel tradition involving winter leagues and an alumni tournament, described as a 'beginning of life-long devotion' for many.
cards.access_notes: Games typically occur in the evenings from January through February.

cards.title: Festival of Christmas
cards.subtitle: A 70-year musical celebration of Advent
cards.notes: Attend this massive multi-choir and orchestral performance in Benson Great Hall, featuring a candlelight processional and sacred music.
cards.short_summary: An annual Christmas performance featuring over 300 student musicians, a tradition that has run for 70 years.
cards.evidence_claim: The Festival of Christmas is in its 70th year as of 2026, featuring a candlelight processional and performances by various Bethel choirs and ensembles.
cards.access_notes: Requires tickets; usually held the first weekend of December.

cards.title: The High-Energy Move-In
cards.subtitle: Upperclassmen 'herds' greeting new students
cards.notes: Watch as energetic student volunteers dance and haul luggage to dorm rooms to welcome the incoming class. It is a signature high-energy start.
cards.short_summary: A decades-old tradition where upperclassmen volunteers energetically assist new students with moving into their residence halls.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Week move-in involves 'herds of caffeinated upperclass student volunteers dancing energetically as they unpack new students' cars.'
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in late August during the first days of Welcome Week.

cards.title: Finals Week Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Late-night fuel before exams
cards.notes: Head to the Dining Center at 11:45 p.m. during finals week for a late-night meal served by faculty and staff to celebrate the semester's end.
cards.short_summary: A finals week tradition where students gather for a late-night breakfast served by university staff to relieve exam stress.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Breakfast is a finals week tradition held from 11:45 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. in the dining commons.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night (11:45 PM) during finals week in the Monson Dining Center.

cards.title: Core Group Family Units
cards.subtitle: Small group bonding for new students
cards.notes: Join your assigned 'family unit' of 15 students led by upperclassmen to navigate your first week and build immediate community connections.
cards.short_summary: Small orientation groups, known as Core Groups, that serve as a primary social unit for new students during Welcome Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Core Groups are described as a 'Welcome Week family unit' including about 15 other students led by upper-class students.
cards.access_notes: Specific to new students during orientation week.

cards.title: Last Day Cookie Tent
cards.subtitle: Fresh cookies and cocoa on the patio
cards.notes: Visit the Brushaber Commons patio on the last day of fall classes for free freshly baked cookies and hot cocoa, often featuring a visit from Santa.
cards.short_summary: An annual event on the last day of classes where the dining service provides free cookies and treats to students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sodexo Cookie Tent is an annual event on the last day of classes featuring freshly baked cookies and hot cocoa on the BC Patio.
cards.access_notes: Typically held from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on the final day of fall semester classes.

cards.title: Spring Fling Mocktails
cards.subtitle: End-of-year outdoor celebration
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the spring semester with mocktails, frozen yogurt, and photo booths at the CLC Circle. Arrive early for free treats.
cards.short_summary: A year-end social event for students featuring outdoor activities, non-alcoholic drinks, and community bonding.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Fling features mocktails, frozen yogurt, and a photobooth at the CLC Circle, sponsored by Bethel Student Government.
cards.access_notes: Held in May; rain plan moves the event inside Brushaber Commons.

cards.title: The Wildcat Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Igniting school spirit behind the stadium
cards.notes: Gather behind the stadium during Homecoming weekend for a massive bonfire to rally support for the Royals. It is a classic fall spirit event.
cards.short_summary: A traditional bonfire held during Homecoming weekend to build community and school spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wildcat Bonfire is a scheduled event during Homecoming, typically held behind the stadium.
cards.access_notes: Open to students and alumni during Homecoming weekend, usually in October.

cards.title: Vespers Under the Lights
cards.subtitle: Outdoor worship at Royal Stadium
cards.notes: Experience a special outdoor edition of the Vespers service held under the stadium lights to kick off the fall semester. It is a new campus tradition.
cards.short_summary: A recently established tradition of holding the first Vespers service of the fall semester outdoors at the football stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The first Vespers service of the fall semester is now held under the new lights at Royal Stadium, marking a 'fresh space to gather.'
cards.source_title: Vespers under the lights: a fresh space to gather and grow
cards.access_notes: Held annually in September at Royal Stadium.
